text.p: Salomon Brothers said in a report released on Tuesday it had raised its 1997 and 1998 EPS estimates for Israel's Teledata Communications and reiterated a buy recommendation after a strong first quarter.
Based on sales visibility, Salomon said it was raising its 1997 EPS forecast to $1.02 from $0.95 and its 1998 EPS estimate to $1.27 from $1.25.
Teledata reported a first quarter 1997 EPS of $0.22 compared with $0.10 for the same period last year.

The report by analyst Victor Halpert said Teledata sales increased by 101 percent year on year, to $19.23 million in the first quarter of 1997 from $9.6 million in the first quarter of 1996. Salomon had expected $18 million in revenues.

"Sales of recently introduced products amounted to more than 58 percent of total revenues," the report said, noting that Teledata's management had indicated that during the first quarter the company had received $21.4 million in new orders.
"Additional major contracts are expected to be announced in the near future," Salomon said.
